title: Cisco Patches 34 Vulnerabilities Across Multiple Products
description: Cisco released patches addressing 34 vulnerabilities across multiple products including Expressway Series, IOS XR, Snort 3, and Unified Communications. The vulnerabilities include critical remote code execution, authentication bypass, and cross-site scripting issues. Notably, a critical remote code execution flaw in Expressway Series could allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root. Other critical issues affect Unified Communications and Snort 3 products. Cisco is not aware of any active exploitation of these vulnerabilities in the wild.
aiSummary: Cisco patched 34 security vulnerabilities spanning Expressway Series, IOS XR, Snort 3, and Unified Communications products. The Expressway Series fixes include a critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-76466) caused by persistent cookies and insufficient client certificate validation, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root. Unified Communications products received patches for multiple critical issues involving improper resource control, authentication, and input validation (CVE-2026-76473, CVE-2026-76474, CVE-2026-76475). Snort 3 patches address critical incorrect calculation and out-of-bounds write vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-20236, CVE-2026-20043) along with other high and medium severity bugs. Additional high-severity flaws include a denial-of-service vulnerability in IOS XR (CVE-2026-76505) and a privilege escalation bug in Secure Client’s Secure Firewall Posture module (CVE-2026-76462). Cisco has released official patches for all these issues and reports no known exploitation in the wild.
aiImpact: Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges, bypass authentication mechanisms, perform cross-site scripting attacks, cause denial-of-service conditions, and escalate privileges on affected Cisco products. These impacts could compromise device integrity, confidentiality, and availability. However, Cisco currently reports no known active exploitation of these vulnerabilities in the wild.
